title: Reid 1985: centroid distance of rectus abdominis at L5 (M, unspecified)

imaging.plane: transverse scans at 0.5-2.0 cm intervals from xiphoid to symphysis pubis, normalised to 15 slices per subject
imaging.level_definition: whole muscle between xiphoid and pubis (average over slices)

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm; distance of muscle from the vertebral centreline divided by AP trunk depth measured at L5 (level of the distance measurement assumed to be L5; not stated explicitly)

source.sample: 28 living subjects (16 M, 12 F); archival CT scans

how_to_simulate: At L5, take the model muscle centroid AP distance from the vertebral body centre (transverse plane).
Divide by the model/subject AP trunk depth at L5 and compare the ratio.
protocol.notes: Dimensionless ratio; the paper calls it the moment-arm ratio (centroid distance, not a true moment arm).

extraction.check_notes: Values verified on rendered pages 279-280. Text prints ES total 31.74 and right 15.72 cm2; Table 2 prints 31.75 and 15.73 (table used).
